overall: Thursday is expected to bring a mixed day for New York City — patchy morning fog clearing to mostly sunny skies, but with a 50% chance of afternoon and evening showers and thunderstorms. The NWS text forecast calls for a high near 84°F, though ensemble model data suggests the actual max may come in considerably lower, around 76–77°F, possibly held down by cloud cover, precipitation, or sea breeze dynamics. Overall a warm, humid summer day with convective uncertainty.
forecast_obs_notes: Model agreement is notably poor and spread is wide. ECMWF is the most bearish at ~71.7°F, GFS and HRRR both land near 74.3°F, while GEM and NBM are higher at ~77–78°F. The forecast-only model (83°F) and NWS narrative (84°F) skew significantly warmer than the observation-anchored ensemble (76.5°F), suggesting the ensemble is being pulled down by yesterday's relatively modest observed max of 75.9°F and potential storm-related cooling. The divergence between NWS/FO and the full ensemble is the dominant uncertainty.
max_temp_prediction: The full ensemble model points to an expected TMAX of 76.5°F, with the active odd-bucket market showing the top probability bucket at 71–72°F (24.9%) and the second bucket at 69–70°F (19.9%), implying meaningful downside risk to the NWS 84°F headline. The Tier 2 rating (good confidence, ~52% expected accuracy) supports leaning toward the 71–72°F odd bucket as the modal outcome. Confidence is moderate — convective storms could suppress the afternoon max well below NWS guidance, but a brief sunny window before storms could push temps toward the mid-to-upper 70s.
